environment.note: This checks whether OSV-Scanner's Go call-graph reachability suppresses a vulnerability alert when the vulnerable symbol is never called — a deterministic pass/fail observation (alert present/absent + a called boolean), not a timing benchmark. CPU/GPU/RAM do not affect the result, so they are intentionally omitted.

subject.name: OSV-Scanner reachability (Go call analysis)
subject.note: osv-scanner v2.4.0 pinned; Go 1.25.5 installed to a temp dir. call-analysis=go is the default for Go modules.

baseline.name: Naive lockfile matching (--no-call-analysis=go)
baseline.note: Reachability is compared against the naive dependency-graph match it refines: same two modules are scanned both ways in the same run, and the comparison is by observed alert presence, not by measured timing.

fixture.design: Two Go modules import the IDENTICAL vulnerable dependency (x/text v0.3.7) and differ only in which function they call: reachable/ calls the flagged ParseAcceptLanguage; unreachable/ calls only language.Make.

raw_artifacts.retention_policy: none discarded — all evidence for this run is small and committed
raw_artifacts.note: The deterministic evidence — probe-result.json (the 2x2 alert matrix plus the experimental_analysis.called boolean for GO-2022-1059) — is committed alongside the two fixture modules. No large raw artifacts are produced.
